newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.

text.p: In the South, rice prices were steady to $.50 per cwt higher.

Long grain milled rice prices were selling mostly at $20.00 per cwt.; Medium grain traded mostly at $18.50-$19.00; Second heads were steady and Brewers remain in very tight supply with few quotes at $14.50-$15.75.

Rice by-products were uneven, bran was steady to $5.00 higher, millfeed was mostly steady to $3.00 Lower. In California, rice prices were steady, with Medium grain selling mostly at $19.00-$19.50 with some discounts down to $18.00. Rice bran was $5.00-$10.00 higher.

California rice ship loadings: For the week ending January 25 at the port of Stockton: The Kenzui loaded 8,900.64 mt of U.S. No. 1 medium grain milled bagged rice and 1,101.24 mt of U.S. No. 1 bagged second heads destined for Japan.
At the port of Sacramento: The Eemsgracht and The Ken Un both loaded 10,000 mt each of U.S. No. 1 medium grain milled bagged rice destined for Japan.
Inspections of California rice for export: For the week ending January 25, there were 661,722 cwt of rice inspected.
The yearly total since October 1, 1996 is 4,743,123 cwt compared to 3,104,865 cwt a year ago.
